# About this script

This script downloads and extracts **climatic** (WorldClim v2.1) and
**soil** (SoilGrids v2.0) predictor variables for a set of geographic
coordinates, checks for **multicollinearity** among predictors, and
exports:

- a predictor table (`data/predictors.xlsx`);
- a correlation matrix (`outputs/corr.txt`);
- a summary table with descriptive statistics (`outputs/summary_var.xlsx`);
- a correlation plot (`figs/correl.tiff`).

# Packages

All packages used are available on CRAN, including `geodata` and
`soilDB`, which download external data (WorldClim and SoilGrids,
respectively) on demand. 

```{r}
# Install 'soilDB' if not already installed
# install.packages('soilDB')
# Load libraries
library(readxl)       # To read Excel files
library(sp)           # For spatial data structures
library(raster)       # To work with raster data
library(foreach)      # For parallel processing
library(doParallel)   # For parallel backend registration
library(tidyverse)    # For data manipulation and visualization
library(Hmisc)        # For correlation and statistical functions
library(corrplot)     # For correlation matrix plotting
library(skimr)        # For summarizing data
library(openxlsx)     # For writing Excel files
library(here)         # To establish the path context
```

# Load data 
We read the coordinate spreadsheet and convert it into a spatial object
(`SpatialPoints`), used in the raster extraction steps below.

```{r}
env <- read_xlsx(here("data/data_ferns.xlsx"), sheet = "e_matrix")

coords <- data.frame(x = env$Long, y = env$Lat) %>%
  `rownames<-`(env$Site) %>%
  SpatialPoints(., proj4string = CRS('+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs'))

```
# Climatic variables rasters

We selected three bioclimatic variables from WorldClim v2.1
(2.5 arc-minute resolution, ~21 km² at the equator):

| WorldClim code     | Abbrev. | Description                                       |
|--------------------|---------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| bio_12             | AP      | Annual Precipitation                                |
| bio_15             | PS      | Precipitation Seasonality                           |
| bio_10             | MT      | Max Temperature of Warmest Quarter                    |

Rasters are downloaded automatically by the `geodata` package on first
run and cached in `gis/worldclim/`; subsequent runs reuse the local cache
(`download = TRUE` only downloads files that are not already present).

```{r}
bio <- geodata::worldclim_global(
  path = here("gis/worldclim"),
  var = "bio",
  res = 2.5,
  download = T
)

names(bio)

x_var <- bio[[c('wc2.1_2.5m_bio_12', 'wc2.1_2.5m_bio_15', 'wc2.1_2.5m_bio_10')]]
names(x_var) <- c("AP", "PS", "MT")
```

## Extracting climatic values per site

We loop through each of the three raster layers and extract the value
corresponding to each sample site's location.

```{r}
clim <- foreach(i = 1:3) %do%
  {
    raster::extract(x = raster::raster(x_var[[i]]), y = coords)
  } |>
  do.call(what = cbind) |>
  `colnames<-`(c(
    "AP",
    "PS",
    "MT"
  )) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(id = env$Site)
```
# Soil variables (SoilGrids)

We download soil data from SoilGrids (topsoil layer, 0-5 cm depth) for
the same coordinates, for the following variables:

| Abbrev. | Description                                |
|---------|-----------------------------------------------|
| C       | Clay content                                  |
| N       | Nitrogen (total)                              |
| CEC     | Cation Exchange Capacity                      |

```{r}
# SoilGrid
soil <- soilDB::fetchSoilGrids(
  x = env,
  loc.names = c("Site", 'Lat', 'Long'),
  depth_intervals = "0-5",
  variables = c("clay", "nitrogen", "cec")
)
# Select soil mean values and clean column names
var_soil <- dplyr::select(as.data.frame(soil), id, ends_with("mean")) %>%
  `colnames<-`(gsub(colnames(.), pattern = 'mean', replacement = ''))
```

# Merge variables

```{r}
bio <- merge(clim, var_soil, by = "id")
```
# Testing multicollinearity

We rename columns to descriptive names and calculate the Pearson
correlation matrix (coefficients and p-values) among predictors, using
the full spreadsheet (`env`), which also contains sampling effort and
plot size variables.

```{r}
# Rename columns to descriptive names
colnames(bio) <- c(
  'id',
  "Ann. Precipitation",
  "Prec. Seasonality",
  "Max. Temp.",
  "Clay",
  "Nitrogen",
  "CEC"
)
# Calculate correlation matrix and p-values
# correl.b <- rcorr(as.matrix(bio[, -1]))
colnames(env) <- c(
  "Site",
  "Lat",
  "Long", 
  "Ann. Precipitation",
  "Rain. Seasonality",
  "Max. Temp.",
  "Rain. Warmest Q.",
  "Clay",
  "Nitrogen",
  "CEC",
  "Sample Effort",
  "Plot Size"
)
correl.b <- rcorr(as.matrix(env[, -1:-3]))
# Save correlation matrix to file
write.table(correl.b$r, here("outputs/corr.txt"))
write.xlsx(bio, here("data/predictors.xlsx"))


```

## Summary statistics

We generate descriptive statistics (mean, SD, min, max, etc.) for each
predictor and save them to Excel.


```{r}
# Create summary table
# Generate summary statistics (mean, SD, etc.)
summary_var <- skim(bio[, -1]) |>
  mutate(
    skim_variable = c(
      "Annual Precipitation Mean (mm)",
      "Precipitation Seasonality (%CV)",
      "Max. Temperature in Warmest Quarter (C*100)",
      "Clay (g/100g)",
      "Nitrogen (cg/kg)",
      "Cation Exchange Capacity (cmol(c)/kg)"
    )
  )
# Save summary statistics to Excel
write.xlsx(summary_var, here("outputs/summary_var.xlsx"))

```


## Correlation plot

We generate a correlation matrix plot (upper triangle only), with
non-significant cells (p > 0.05) left blank.

```{r}
tiff(
  filename = here("figs/correl.tiff"),
  width = 180,
  height = 180,
  units = "mm",
  res = 600
)
corrplot(
  correl.b$r,
  type = "upper",
  method= 'number',
  order = "hclust",
  p.mat = correl.b$P,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  insig = "blank"
)

dev.off()
```
